skill.name: forensics-osquery
skill.description: Use osquery for endpoint forensic investigation, incident response, and threat hunting. The skill provides read-only query workflows, detection packs, and deployment references for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
skill.summary: Investigate endpoint activity with osquery queries and defensive forensic packs.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: I found no prompt injection or hidden automation in the reviewed files. Most static findings are defensive osquery queries, Markdown examples, or administrator deployment guidance. The main remaining risk is that authorized osquery use can expose sensitive endpoint data.

remediation.issue: Sensitive forensic output can include secrets, account data, and process memory indicators.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent, scoping, encryption, retention, and redaction requirements before collecting or sharing results.

remediation.issue: Privileged setup and execution examples require root or administrator access.
remediation.suggestion: Label privileged commands as manual administrator actions and recommend lab validation before production use.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md references helper scripts that are not included in the scanned files.
remediation.suggestion: Add the scripts or remove those references so users do not rely on unavailable automation.

content.value_statement: Security teams need fast endpoint evidence without switching tools. This skill provides osquery workflows, packs, and references for focused forensic collection.
actual_capabilities: Guides live endpoint triage with osquery process, network, user, and file tables.
Provides defensive query packs for triage, persistence, lateral movement, and credential-access detection.
Maps many hunting queries to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
Explains osqueryd deployment, scheduling, logging, and fleet management concepts.
Documents platform differences for Linux, macOS, and Windows investigations.
limitations: Requires osquery to be installed and accessible on the target endpoint.
Some workflows require root or administrator privileges.
Query results need analyst review before incident conclusions are made.
Referenced helper scripts are not included in the scanned files.

use_cases.title: Triage a Suspected Endpoint Compromise
use_cases.description: Collect process, login, network, and persistence evidence with read-only osquery queries.

use_cases.title: Build Threat Hunting Queries
use_cases.description: Convert a suspected behavior into osquery SQL mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

use_cases.title: Plan Continuous osqueryd Monitoring
use_cases.description: Create scheduled query packs and logging guidance for endpoint monitoring at fleet scale.

prompt_templates.title: Run Initial Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Run initial triage on a Linux endpoint using osquery. Focus on processes, logged-in users, listening ports, and recent persistence changes.

prompt_templates.title: Hunt Windows Persistence
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Windows persistence hunt with osquery. Include registry Run keys, scheduled tasks, services, and WMI event consumers.

prompt_templates.title: Map Behaviors to ATT&CK
prompt_templates.prompt: Map suspicious PowerShell and credential-access behavior to MITRE ATT&CK. Create osquery hunts and explain expected evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Design Fleet Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe osqueryd monitoring plan for 500 mixed endpoints. Include query intervals, data handling controls, and tuning guidance.

output_examples.input: Investigate a server with unusual outbound connections.
output_examples.output: A triage plan covering active sockets, owning processes, listening ports, login sessions, and follow-up pivots.

output_examples.input: Create a hunt for suspected persistence on macOS.
output_examples.output: A set of launchd, startup item, shell profile, and browser extension checks with analyst review notes.

output_examples.input: Prepare osqueryd monitoring for an incident response team.
output_examples.output: Recommended query packs, schedule intervals, logging controls, and safeguards for sensitive endpoint data.

best_practices: Run queries with approved authorization and record the investigative scope.
Store exported results in encrypted evidence storage with access controls.
Test expensive or broad queries in a lab before production use.
anti_patterns: Running broad endpoint queries without a defined incident scope.
Sharing raw query output that contains secrets or personal data.
Deploying scheduled packs without performance testing and retention limits.

faq.question: Does this skill install osquery?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You must install and approve osquery separately.

faq.question: Can it run on Linux, macOS, and Windows?
faq.answer: Yes, the references include platform-specific notes. Some tables only work on certain operating systems.

faq.question: Does it collect sensitive data?
faq.answer: It can guide queries that expose sensitive endpoint metadata. Use authorization, encryption, and redaction controls.

faq.question: Are the query packs ready for production?
faq.answer: They are useful starting points. Tune intervals, filters, and retention for your environment.

faq.question: Does it include executable helper scripts?
faq.answer: No executable scripts were present in the scanned files. The skill references scripts that are not included.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is best for incident responders, threat hunters, and security engineers familiar with endpoint investigations.
